idiom_name: Spring Security method security - @EnableMethodSecurity with @PreAuthorize("hasRole('X')")/hasAuthority, GrantedAuthority from a UserDetailsService, RoleHierarchy bean for inheritance
implementation_notes: The JVM's dominant realization is Spring Security. Enable method security once with @EnableMethodSecurity and annotate the decision points - @PreAuthorize("hasRole('PAUSER')") for a single role, @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('MINTER','ADMIN')") for alternatives, @PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('token:pause')") for a permission-style authority - or declare the same rules centrally in authorizeHttpRequests(). Membership arrives as GrantedAuthority objects on the Authentication, loaded by a UserDetailsService from a role table or by a JwtAuthenticationConverter from claims; role inheritance is a RoleHierarchy bean (ROLE_ADMIN > ROLE_PAUSER), applied by the RoleHierarchyVoter so a senior role inherits junior permissions without duplicate grants. Deny-by-default is configured, not assumed: end the request matcher chain with .anyRequest().authenticated() (or .denyAll()). Roles are data managed by your own service (or Spring's group support) and should be auditable. JAAS Subjects/roles and Jakarta Security offer the same seam at the application-server layer.
pitfalls: hasRole('ADMIN') implicitly prepends the ROLE_ prefix, so an authority stored as ADMIN_HIGH or admin never matches; keep the prefix convention consistent between storage and expression.

@PreAuthorize is enforced by a proxy: a call from inside the same bean (self-invocation) bypasses it, and it does not apply to private or final methods - keep the annotated method on the boundary the caller reaches.
Authorities decoded from a JWT are a snapshot; a revoked role stays valid until the token expires, so keep tokens short or resolve roles from the database per request.
A RoleHierarchy bean without the RoleHierarchyVoter configured changes nothing; confirm the voter is in the chain so the hierarchy actually resolves.
Hiding a UI control is not authorization - the method or HTTP rule must enforce the operation.
